title: Was the Single Shared Trace Log Successfully Implemented? Root-Cause Review

tldr.content:
Partially implemented. The single-log *location* is correctly shipped and worktree-independent: from any linked worktree the default is `<main-repo-root>/.agents/logs/trace.jsonl` (experiment-verified).

But traces are not actually pushed to it automatically: nothing calls the recorder for ordinary actions (`recordDecision` has zero production callers; only `wt-session` calls `appendTrace`), so the shared log holds just 4 records while activity is untraced — and the old `.git/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` and a legacy per-run file still exist, so history is split rather than single.

Root cause: the shipped work implemented the log's location/override/concurrency/durability, not an automatic action/decision recording hook; `AGENTS.md` instructs agents to record traces, but no mechanism triggers or enforces it.

executiveSummary.content:
Question: was the change to route action/decision traces to ONE shared per-repo log successfully implemented, and if not, why?

```text

intent (AGENTS.md): record every action + decision via scripts/lib/trace-log.mjs

  shipped:      location override + concurrency + durability + wt-session writers

  not shipped:  an automatic recording hook for ordinary agent/build actions

  result:       one DEFAULT path exists, but it stays nearly empty; old logs remain

```

Headline evidence: (a) the default path resolves to the main root's `.agents/logs/trace.jsonl` from a linked worktree [ref-repo-state][ref-experiments]; (b) the only production writer is `wt-session` and `recordDecision` is unused [ref-wt-session][ref-trace-log]; (c) three trace files exist on disk and the old `<git-common-dir>` log was explicitly never migrated [ref-experiments][ref-plan-location]; and (d) both plans are marked complete because their scope was the location/registry, not a recorder [ref-plan-shared][ref-plan-location].

Headline caveats: Jev is advisory only and corroborates, never proves [ref-jev-diagnosis][ref-jev-judge]; the relative-path escape is a real but secondary defect [ref-repo-state]; and no plan ever promised an automatic hook, so this is a gap between `AGENTS.md`'s stated intent and the wired implementation [ref-agents-md][ref-plan-location].

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported - The default single-log path is implemented and worktree-independent: `<main-repo-root>/.agents/logs/trace.jsonl`. [ref-repo-state][ref-experiments][ref-tests-trace-log]

K2. supported - Tracing is not automatic: `recordDecision` has zero production callers; only `scripts/wt-session.mjs` calls `appendTrace` (create/merge/nuke/cleanup); no harness hook exists. [ref-wt-session][ref-trace-log][ref-agents-md]

K3. supported - The shared log is nearly empty relative to activity: 4 records (2 manual csm-build, 2 wt-session cleanup). [ref-experiments]

K4. supported - Three trace files exist on disk; the old `.git/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` was deliberately never migrated. [ref-experiments][ref-plan-location]

K5. supported - The legacy per-run fallback in `wt-session.mjs` is unreachable dead code. [ref-wt-session]

K6. partially-supported - A relative configured `traceLogPath` can escape the repo root, contrary to the docs (root-depth-dependent example; the escape itself is the defect). [ref-repo-state][ref-experiments][ref-docs-traces]

K7. partially-supported - An invalid config layer yields the default path; a refusing-to-write nuance, not the layer-fallthrough contradiction first suspected. [ref-trace-config][ref-tests-trace-config]

K8. supported - Root cause: the shipped work delivered path/override/concurrency/durability, not automatic recording; `AGENTS.md` intends recording but nothing triggers it; the un-migrated old log is a minor by-design contributor. [ref-agents-md][ref-wt-session]

K9. partially-supported - Jev advisory: `default_path_only` + `no_automatic_hook` (confidence 1.0), draft rubric factual 0.72 / citation 0.65 / completeness 0.97 / clarity 0.67; corroborating, never a gate. [ref-jev-diagnosis][ref-jev-judge]

detailSections.content:
## D1. What actually shipped

`repo-state.mjs:93-98` resolves the default to `<mainRepoRoot>/.agents/logs/trace.jsonl` and honours an absolute `configured` override; `trace-log.mjs` appends one redacted, UTC, bounded line per record with a single `O_APPEND` write; `trace-config.mjs` resolves `CSM_TRACE_LOG` > project `.csm-skills.json` > user `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/csm/skills.json` > default [ref-repo-state][ref-trace-log][ref-trace-config]. Tests cover the default, linked-worktree persistence, and precedence [ref-tests-trace-log][ref-tests-trace-config].

```text

linked worktree cwd -> repoMainRoot() = main checkout

                   -> repoLogPath()  = <main>/.agents/logs/trace.jsonl   (experiment E1)

```

## D2. Why it looks unimplemented

The only production caller of the recorder is `scripts/wt-session.mjs:99` inside `appendSessionTrace`, invoked for worktree create/merge/nuke/cleanup events [ref-wt-session]. `recordDecision` has no production caller [ref-trace-log]. There is no hook in `.lefthook.yml`, the pre-commit script, or the orchestrator that records ordinary actions or decisions. The on-disk log confirms it: 4 records total [ref-experiments], while a whole session's actions produced none.

```mermaid

flowchart LR

  act[agent action / decision] -.->|no hook| nothing[no trace]

  wts[wt-session create/merge/nuke/cleanup] --> trace[appendTrace -> shared log]

```

## D3. Split history (multiple logs)

Three files exist: the current `.agents/logs/trace.jsonl`; the legacy per-run `.agents/logs/2026-09-20-wt-session-trace.jsonl`; and the old-design `.git/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` [ref-experiments]. The trace-location plan recorded as an unresolved risk that the old `<git-common-dir>` log is not auto-migrated [ref-plan-location], so go-forward is a single default path but history is not unified.

## D4. Secondary defects

A relative configured path escapes the repo (`join` normalizes `..`), contradicting the operator doc [ref-repo-state][ref-docs-traces][ref-experiments]. The `wt-session` per-run fallback is unreachable dead code [ref-wt-session]. An invalid config layer yields the default path rather than refusing to write [ref-trace-config][ref-tests-trace-config].

## D5. Root cause

The three shipped plans scoped themselves to the log's location, override precedence, concurrency, and durability, and the registry migration [ref-plan-shared][ref-plan-location]. None included an automatic action/decision recording hook. `AGENTS.md` states the intent to record actions and decisions via the trace log [ref-agents-md], but that intent is an instruction to the model with no trigger, guard, or enforcement, so in practice traces are not pushed to the single log. The old-log split is a minor by-design contributor, not the primary cause.

recommendation.content:
Treat the change as partially shipped: the single-log *path/config/durability* is done and verified; the *recording* is not. To make traces actually land in the one log:

1. Add an automatic recording seam (a small `trace` CLI or harness hook) that emits an action trace at each skill lifecycle transition and a decision trace where a decision is justified, using the existing `appendTrace`/`recordDecision` APIs; keep it best-effort and fail-open like the current writer.

2. Make `AGENTS.md`'s recording instruction enforceable: name the exact command/entry point, or wire it into the lifecycle, so ordinary sessions produce traces rather than relying on the model to remember.

3. Migrate or explicitly retire the old `<git-common-dir>/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` and the legacy per-run file so there is genuinely one log; the plan already documents a concatenate command — run it or mark the old file archived.

4. Fix the relative-path escape by resolving a relative `configured` path against the main root with containment (reject `..` or verify the result stays under the repo), and make the invalid-config case refuse rather than silently default.

5. Remove the dead per-run fallback in `wt-session.mjs` (or convert it into a record of the failure) so the single-log invariant cannot regress.

Confidence: HIGH on the partial-implementation diagnosis and the root cause (multiple independent evidence sources: code, on-disk state, history, sandbox experiment, and an advisory Jev call). Cost of being wrong is low: the fixes are additive and the current path/durability guarantees are unchanged.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. unverifiable - Exactly how many actions/decisions the user expected to see traced, and whether an automatic hook was an intended deliverable. The three plans do not list it, so intent is inferred from AGENTS.md.

U2. partially-supported - Whether the old `.git/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` should be migrated or archived is an operator decision; the finding records that it exists and is not written, not which disposition is correct.

U3. partially-supported - Jev's `multiple_live_logs` answer (0.71) and its root-cause choice are advisory single-sample classifications over a summarized state, corroborated but not proven by the code evidence.

U4. unverifiable - Whether any external harness (outside this repo) consumes the trace log and would break if recording became automatic.

claims.statement: The single shared trace-log DEFAULT path is implemented and worktree-independent: repoLogPath resolves to <main-repo-root>/.agents/logs/trace.jsonl from any linked worktree.

Action/decision tracing is not automatic: recordDecision has zero production callers and the only production caller of appendTrace is scripts/wt-session.mjs (worktree create/merge/nuke/cleanup); no harness hook records ordinary agent actions.

As a consequence the shared log is nearly empty relative to activity: .agents/logs/trace.jsonl holds four records (two manual csm-build task-complete lines and two wt-session cleanup lines) while many session actions are untraced.

More than one trace file exists on disk and the old log was deliberately never migrated: .git/csm/logs/trace.jsonl (old <git-common-dir> design, two records), .agents/logs/2026-09-20-wt-session-trace.jsonl (legacy per-run), and .agents/logs/trace.jsonl (current).

scripts/wt-session.mjs retains the legacy per-run fallback path, but it is unreachable: appendTrace and repoLogPath are acquired in the same try, and appendSessionTrace early-returns when appendTrace is null, so the ternary always takes the shared-log branch.

A relative configured traceLogPath can escape the repository root because repoLogPath uses path.join(mainRoot, configured) and join normalizes '..', contrary to docs/action-traces-and-cleanup.md which says a relative value stays under the repo root; the number of '..' segments needed depends on root depth, but the escape itself is the defect.

An invalid (malformed/non-CSM) config layer yields null and the writer then uses the default path rather than a less-specific layer; this is a nuance about refusing-to-write, not the documented layer-fallthrough contradiction first suspected.

Root cause of the perceived failure: the shipped work implemented the log's location, override precedence, concurrency, and durability, but not automatic action/decision recording; AGENTS.md instructs agents to record traces but nothing triggers or enforces it, so traces are not pushed to the single log in ordinary sessions, and the deliberately un-migrated old log adds a minor by-design split.

Jev (advisory, via the shipped consult seam over the registered deep-research-judge-* points) classifies the state as 'default_path_only' and the root cause as 'no_automatic_hook' with confidence 1.0, and scores the draft factual 0.72 / citation 0.65 / completeness 0.97 / clarity 0.67 on a 0-1 normalization; this corroborates but does not prove the finding and is never a gate.
